name: ema200_dip_reversal_v1
author: claude_strategist
mechanism: When NIFTY dips to its 60-minute EMA — a major intraday reference level explicitly tracked by index futures desks, VWAP-algo overlays, and delta-hedging market makers — resting buy orders cluster just above this EMA because systematic programs treat it as a 'buy zone' for intraday mean reversion. Each time NIFTY touches this level and holds, the absorption becomes faster as confirmation builds across desks; at 5-second resolution we can detect the first recovery bar (positive 5s return) the moment price re-crosses above the EMA touch zone, entering CE options before the broader 1-minute bar even closes. The 60-minute EMA compresses the original multi-day EMA concept to an intraday one because at 5s resolution with 15-90s hold times we are capturing the institutional intraday reversion, not a multi-day trend recovery. This strategy is intentionally long-biased — PE entries require fewer conditions due to the underlying bullish structural assumption. The EMA dip-reversal mechanism describes institutional buy order clustering at the 60-min EMA; the analogous short-side setup (EMA resistance fades) requires a different signal structure and is outside the scope of this strategy.

indicators.name: ema_720
indicators.purpose: 60-minute EMA at 5s bars (720 × 5s = 3600s). NOT the original 200×12=2400 blind scaling. Rationale: the original EMA200-5min is a multi-day (~17hr) trend support level that is practically impossible to compute reliably within a single trading day's data window. At 5s resolution with 15-90s hold times, the relevant support is INTRADAY — the 60-min EMA represents 3600 seconds of exponentially-weighted price history, sufficient to capture the dominant intraday trend anchor while requiring only a 60-min warmup (signals from ~10:15 IST). The 60-min EMA is the highest-order SAME-SESSION support level visible in a single day's data.

indicators.name: dist_pct
indicators.purpose: Signed percentage distance from the EMA. Positive = above EMA, negative = below. Used to define 'touch zone' (|dist_pct| < ema_touch_pct) and to detect whether price is approaching from above vs. already broken down.

indicators.name: ret_1
indicators.purpose: Single-bar 5-second return. Detects the precise moment price begins recovering at the EMA — the first positive 5s bar after the dip is the earliest possible entry, capturing more of the bounce than waiting for a full 1-min bar.

indicators.name: mom_6
indicators.purpose: 30-second momentum (6 × 5s bars). Guards against entering into a trending breakdown — if 30s momentum is still sharply negative, the dip is a trend break, not a bounce. Chosen to match the minimum hold time (15-30s) so that we require positive momentum at the same timescale we plan to exit.

indicators.name: prior_min_dist
indicators.purpose: Rolling minimum distance from EMA over prior 20 minutes (240 bars). Proxies the original strategy's 'multi-day support' condition: if price has not come within 2× the touch threshold in the last 20 minutes, this is the first approach and may be a breakout, not a tested support. We require at least one prior test within 20 minutes to confirm the EMA is acting as support.

conditions: |dist_pct| < ema_touch_pct (price within touch zone of EMA)
dist_pct[i-1] >= -ema_touch_pct (was at or above EMA on prior bar — not already broken)
ret_1 > bounce_threshold (current 5s bar is positive — bounce starting)
mom_6 > -0.0003 (30s trend not in sharp breakdown)
prior_min_dist < 2 * ema_touch_pct (EMA was tested within last 20 min — confirmed support)
buy_ce.confirmation: First positive 5s bar as price re-touches the EMA from above

conditions: NOT_APPLICABLE — strategy is intentionally long-biased; no PE entries are taken
The EMA dip-reversal thesis (buy orders clustering at 60-min EMA) applies exclusively to the bullish direction
buy_pe.confirmation: Not traded — original was long-only EMA bounce. PE side omitted intentionally per directional_bias=bullish.

exit.stop_rationale: 4 option pts = ~8 NIFTY spot pts at ATM delta ~0.5. If NIFTY falls 8 pts below the 60-min EMA touch zone within 90s, the level has definitively broken and the bounce thesis has failed. Per the reference table, a 30-60s move of 8+ spot pts is a genuine breakdown, not noise (typical 30s range is 2-5 option pts; anything beyond is directional).
exit.target_rationale: 7 option pts = ~14 NIFTY spot pts at delta ~0.5. NIFTY EMA bounces within a session typically return 12-20 spot pts above the touch point within 60-90s as the resting buy orders absorb selling; 7 option pts captures the conservative lower end (1:1.75 R:R vs 4pt stop). This calibrated to typical 1-minute NIFTY moves of 3-7 option pts — our 90s time window should deliver at least that.

filters.vix_filter: vix < 20.0 (regime filter — in high-vol regimes EMA breaks are more likely to become trend breaks rather than bounce-and-recover)
filters.time_filter: 09:35–15:20 IST (skip first 20 min of noisy pre-trend; skip last 10 min of EOD unwinding)
filters.volume_filter: none (NIFTY index volume is noisy at 5s; replaced by prior_touch as support confirmation)
filters.trend_filter: 30s momentum (mom_6) must not be deeply negative

edge.edge_decay_risk: medium — EMA support bounces become less reliable if algorithmic strategies that defend the level reduce their exposure

adaptation_notes: Original EMA200-5min (~17hr lookback) compressed to EMA720-5s (60-min) for intraday use — original period is impractical to compute intraday and misaligned with 15-90s hold times. Multi-day support condition replaced by rolling-min prior_touch within the current session (20-minute look-back). Relative volume filter dropped — NIFTY index volume at 5s is too noisy; prior EMA test acts as a similar confirmation. Long-only preserved (bearish EMA bounces require different setup). VIX threshold kept near original (19→20).
weaknesses: Signals only start ~60 minutes after open (720-bar warmup) — misses morning session
EMA(720) is an intraday construct; on days where overnight gap creates an unusual open, the EMA may not yet reflect the day's dominant trend direction
Prior touch filter with 20-min window may reject valid first-bounce entries on range expansion days
